title: Tasks — DexArena
text: Simulation benchmark Task catalog 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level environments, all verified against the current SoftHandGrasping codebase. 10 sequences 30 stages All Household Industrial Laboratory Office Search 01 Household · 3 stages Meal Preparation Open a lunch box, place bread on a plate, then use a spoon to scoop and transfer a tomato. Explore task ↗ 02 Household · 4 stages Cabinet & Pouring Open a cabinet, retrieve and place a bottle, unscrew and place its cap, then pour the contents into a bowl. Explore task ↗ 03 Household · 3 stages Drawer & Plug Open the middle drawer, retrieve a charger, place it on the table, and align both prongs into a socket. Explore task ↗ 04 Industrial · 3 stages Nut & Bolt Stand a bolt upright, seat a nut on its axis, then rotate the nut counterclockwise through a full half turn. Explore task ↗ 05 Office · 3 stages Office Desk Open a laptop, type the target word followed by Enter, and complete the sequence with a left mouse click. Explore task ↗ 06 Industrial · 3 stages Furniture Assembly Lay a panel flat, slide a rail into its groove, and fasten it by turning a wing screw by hand. Explore task ↗ 07 Laboratory · 2 stages Pipette Transfer Aspirate from a sample cup, return the pipette, then dispense into a target well and return it again. Explore task ↗ 08 Household · 5 stages Juice Preparation Open a refrigerator, move an apple into a blender, close the door, place the lid, and press the power button. Explore task ↗ 09 Household · 2 stages Package Opening Open both package flaps with two hands, then extract the apple and place it stably on the plate. Explore task ↗ 10 Household · 2 stages Table Cleaning Pick three debris blocks into a dustpan, then tip all three into a trash bin. Explore task ↗

Open a topic for track definitions, metric details or reproducibility requirements. 01 Evaluation tracks & native scenes 30 stages, three kitchens and ten complete sequences DexArena separates failures in execution, generalization and composition while preserving matching task definitions. 01 · Stage level Skill execution Run each of the 30 canonical stage environments with its registered robot, horizon, action layout and physical success predicate. 50 evaluation episodes per stage in the training scene Each stage starts from its own valid reset distribution Persistent success, not transient contact 29-D single-arm or 58-D bimanual Sharpa actions 02 · Scene level Visual generalization Evaluate every stage on three native scene surfaces using identical object placement and the fixed 256 × 256 policy camera rig. 30 stages × 3 native scenes × 50 episodes 90 task × scene combinations Freeze the policy; no further adaptation Retain the background manifest for every run 03 · Sequence level Skill composition Execute two to five dependent stages in their parent long-horizon environment and report complete-sequence success. 10 sequences × 50 episodes Stage progress and terminal success Reset once per episode; inherited state between stages Single-arm and bimanual tasks The canonical data and reported scores use Panda arms with Sharpa hands. Simulation also supports parallel-jaw grippers, Wuji and XHand, with embodiment-specific action spaces; that support does not imply a scored result matrix for each end-effector. One task. Three native scenes. The same pipette workstation in blue stone, light wood and warm wood kitchens. All 30 stages are evaluated across these three native backgrounds with fixed policy cameras and shared task definitions. Keep task horizons and physical success predicates fixed; persistent hold counters and latches are part of the task definition. For cross-scene results, average stage success within each scene first, then report the mean and standard deviation across the three scene averages. The ± value is scene variation, not a training-seed confidence interval. 03 Episode protocol & stage transitions Evaluation seeds, frozen policies and transitions without resets All six baselines use image observations and robot proprioception, with matched task horizons, randomization and embodiments. Stage and long-horizon success are measured over 50 episodes per task; generalization uses 50 episodes in each of three held-out kitchens without further adaptation. Recorded evaluation seeds The manuscript specifies stage seeds 50000–50049 for ACT and DP. GR00T uses 10001–10050, reused for each generalization scene and the long-horizon protocol. Record the seed manifest alongside each result. New comparison sweeps should use matched episode seeds across methods; do not imply the manuscript used identical seed ranges for every method. The same frozen policy and episode-seed range are reused across native scenes within the corresponding evaluation run. Transitions without resets PPO, RLPD, ACT, DP and π0.5 switch between learned stage policies when the stage succeeds. GR00T uses one task model trained on pooled stage data, with a new instruction at each transition. Do not reset simulator state between stages of a complete sequence. title: DexArena documentation — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / DexArena documentation DexArena documentation Install the released benchmark, inspect replay-validated data, and train and evaluate dexterous policies. From an environment to an auditable result DexArena brings together 10 long-horizon tasks, 30 stage tasks and four end effectors . Each complete sequence has physically grounded success predicates; a stage measures one skill, while a long task preserves the scene across skill transitions. The released demonstrations and the manuscript results use Franka arms with Sharpa hands. New to the benchmark? Follow the OpenCabinet tutorial from installation to a checkpoint evaluation. Use the task catalog for visual stage definitions and the Leaderboard for the unchanged manuscript scores and their evaluation protocol. 01 · SET UP Installation Python, simulator, GPU drivers, dataset access and object meshes. 02 · INSPECT Data & replay Download one task and distinguish state restoration from action replay. 03 · TRAIN Six baseline recipes Prepare policy inputs and run the released training entry points. 04 · EVALUATE Checkpoints & protocol Match cameras, runtime, seeds and horizons before comparing results. What is available now Artifact Official location Scope Code Public benchmark repository ↗ Tasks, robots, data tools, training and evaluation code; consult the repository license. Demonstrations SIPAIR/DexArena · gated access ↗ 3,000 released episodes: 100 replay-successful demonstrations for each of 30 Sharpa stage tasks. Meshes Dataset repository · assets/ ↗ Object meshes downloaded separately into tasks/assets/ . Checkpoints Dataset repository · ckpt/ ↗ ACT, Diffusion Policy, PPO, RLPD, GR00T N1.7 and π0.5; model-specific runtimes and access terms apply. Paper arXiv:2611.02629 ↗ Public preprint and copyable citation . Community evaluation Reproduction checklist Public leaderboard submission intake is not open. Access is gated; the download endpoint is public Request access once on the Hugging Face dataset page, then run hf auth login . Access is granted automatically after the request. Model backbones such as Cosmos may require separate approval. Start with one dataset or checkpoint rather than downloading the whole Hub repository. A practical reading order Install and confirm that import tasks registers the environments. Download and validate a stage dataset, preserving its integrity certificate and raw replay recordings. Render the policy cameras and train , or go straight to a released checkpoint . Evaluate with the checkpoint's observation contract and the declared horizon. Keep episode records before aggregating. Record provenance , then cite the benchmark and methods . Three tracks, different questions Track Evaluation unit What it measures Stage execution 30 stages · 50 episodes per stage An individual skill from its stage reset distribution. Cross-scene transfer 30 stages × 3 native kitchens The same frozen policy across held-out backgrounds; report mean ± scene standard deviation. Long-horizon composition 10 complete tasks · 50 episodes per task Complete-sequence success after one initial reset, with no resets between stages. Code supports Sharpa , Wuji , XHand and Gripper , using <Task>-<Hand>-v1 IDs. This does not imply published scores or datasets for every hand. The live registry is listed in Task table ↗ . Older website task descriptions and checkpoint directories can retain manuscript-era environment names. For executable commands, resolve the current release ID in the public task table; do not rename a checkpoint package to infer its controller binding. Release notes are not new benchmark scores These guides incorporate the maintainers' 9 November 2026 release-validation notes and the current public source interfaces. Timings, sizes and short functional runs are examples from a single workstation, not performance guarantees or replacement leaderboard results. The website does not run simulator, training or evaluation jobs in your browser. Record your code commit, dataset revision and checkpoint hash. A source update can change fingerprints or interfaces; use the release's documented lineage handling instead of bypassing validation. For current code details, begin with Getting started ↗ . title: Installation — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Installation Installation Create the Python environment, download task meshes, and check the public environment registry. Requirements Linux, conda and an NVIDIA GPU with a working Vulkan driver. CPU physics still needs a GPU renderer for image observations. The release setup uses Python 3.10, ManiSkill 3.0.1, SAPIEN 3.0.3, gymnasium 0.29.1, PyTorch 2.7.1 and LeRobot 0.4.0. Keep the repository's current dependency guidance alongside the commands below. Task meshes require about 0.11 GB. The OpenCabinet dataset is about 176 MB; all 30 released datasets total about 10 GB. Download checkpoints individually; their sizes are listed in Evaluation . Source: Installation guide ↗ . Run the following commands from a terminal, not from the website. 1. Clone and create the environment git clone https://github.com/SIPAIR-Elastic/DexArena.git cd DexArena conda create -n ms3 python=3.10 conda activate ms3 python -m pip install datasets "lerobot==0.4.0" python -m pip install --upgrade mani_skill "gymnasium==0.29.1" tyro swanlab h5py tensorboard coacd LeRobot installs PyTorch. The release notes used the CUDA 12.6 default wheel; RTX 50-series cards need the CUDA 12.8 build for compute capability 12.0: python -m pip install torch==2.7.1+cu128 torchvision==0.22.1+cu128 torchaudio==2.7.1+cu128 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 Keep the compatible versions Retain gymnasium==0.29.1 : the release-validation run found that gymnasium 1.x breaks the RLPD evaluation wrapper. PyTorch 2.7.1 is shared by the root, GR00T and OpenPI setups. Record the versions actually installed with your experiment. 2. Request dataset access Demonstrations, task meshes and baseline checkpoints live in SIPAIR/DexArena ↗ . Request access on its page once; the repository grants access automatically. Then log in from the same runtime that will perform the download. Never place your token in a script, URL or shared command log. hf auth login 3. Download task object meshes The meshes are not stored in Git. From the cloned repository root: hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --include "assets/**" --local-dir tasks The resulting directory must be tasks/assets/task_object_meshes/ . The Hugging Face CLI is provided by huggingface_hub , installed with the data dependencies. 4. Check registration and one environment import tasks registers 160 IDs: 40 tasks × four end effectors (Sharpa, Wuji, XHand and Gripper). This is 10 complete tasks and 30 stage tasks per hand, not 160 independently scored manuscript tasks. See Collection targets ↗ and Task table ↗ . import gymnasium as gym import tasks # registers the public task environments env = gym.make( "DrawerPlugOpenDrawer-Sharpa-v1", obs_mode="state", control_mode="pd_joint_pos", ) try: obs, info = env.reset(seed=0) print(env.action_space.shape) # (29,): 7 arm + 22 hand targets obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(env.action_space.sample()) print("success" in info) finally: env.close() Run the public regression suite without downloading demonstrations or checkpoints: python -m pip install pytest python -m pytest tests -q The release maintainers reported 291 passed and two skipped tests on 9 November; your count may change with the code revision. A successful registration or reset is an installation check, not a learned-policy result. 5. Add model-specific runtimes Baseline Runtime Setup PPO, RLPD, ACT, Diffusion Policy The conda environment above Use the scripts and data preparation in Training . GR00T N1.7 libs/Isaac-GR00T/.venv with GR00T, ManiSkill and LeRobot Run bash scripts/groot/setup_env.sh ; it checks out the pinned submodule and uses uv . Dataset conversion also needs ffmpeg . Request separate access to nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2-2B . GR00T guide ↗ π0.5 Python 3.11 virtual environment with pinned OpenPI/JAX Follow OpenPI installation ↗ . Evaluation starts from conda and launches the JAX worker through --policy-python . Troubleshooting and next steps Unregistered ID: run from the cloned repository root and import tasks before gym.make . Vulkan failure: verify the NVIDIA/Vulkan driver independently of the policy, even with physx_cpu . Missing meshes: confirm the download destination in step 3. Continue with the end-to-end tutorial , Data & replay , or the troubleshooting reference . ← Previous DexArena documentation Next → Tutorial: from data to evaluation

title: Data & replay — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Data & replay Data & replay Download a stage dataset, inspect its schema, and verify frame restoration and open-loop action replay separately. What is released The Sharpa demonstrations were teleoperated in simulation, reviewed, exported as LeRobot v3.0 datasets with integrity certificates, and selected by successful action replay. The public pipeline starts at review/export in data_gen/recordings ; the headset/glove teleoperation stack itself is not released. Hub path Contents Approximate size data/sharpa/<env id>/ 100 replay-successful episodes per stage, with multi-view videos 30 datasets · 10 GB total data_append/sharpa/<env id>/ Remaining reviewed state-only episodes where available; together with data/ they partition accepted recordings 2.45 GB total assets/task_object_meshes/ Task object meshes 0.11 GB ckpt/ Baseline checkpoints and release metadata See checkpoint table Get access to SIPAIR/DexArena ↗ , then download one dataset from the code repository root: hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --include "data/sharpa/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1/**" --local-dir . The maintainers' OpenCabinet validation snapshot contains 100 episodes and 13,121 control steps, about 176 MB. Their download time was approximately 90 seconds on one workstation; network and storage conditions vary. Collection context and the public review, validation and rendering pipeline. Dataset layout and policy fields data/sharpa/<env id>/ ├── data/chunk-000/*.parquet # one row per 20 Hz control step ├── videos/observation.images.<camera>/ # base and active-arm wrist cameras ├── meta/info.json, stats.json, tasks.parquet, episodes/ ├── meta/recording_integrity.json # source fingerprint, trim and file hashes ├── meta/subset_manifest.json # release-subset selection ├── meta/video_manifest.json # render counts and image checks └── replay/source_<hash>/ # raw states, actions, infos and reset seed Column Meaning observation.state Robot joint positions/velocities and task quantities. Width and layout depend on the task. action Absolute joint-position targets: 29 for one Sharpa arm and hand, or 58 for both. next.reward 1 while the physical success condition holds, otherwise 0. next.success , next.done Per-step success and episode-end flags. observation.environment_state Flattened simulator state for restoration; names are recorded in meta/info.json. This is not automatically a policy input. The integrity certificate ties recordings to their source build. Current tools resolve explicitly registered equivalent fingerprint lineages before checking compatibility; a genuine fingerprint DRIFT must be investigated, not bypassed. Two checks, two questions Both tools rebuild the recorded environment and consume the raw recordings under replay/source_* . Neither rewrites the training table under data/ . Use the matching code revision and conda environment. Frame restoration Write sampled stored frames into a fresh environment, then compare state, observation, task quantities and rendered images. This tests restoration, not the open-loop stability of the complete action trajectory. python -m data_gen.replay.verify_recording_fidelity --episodes 2 --action-replay \ data/sharpa/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 Inspect nonzero comparison counts on every episode line and a final => FAITHFUL . Solver-contact caches cannot be reconstructed from rigid state alone; excluded quantities are listed as notes. --no-render omits image comparison, --all checks datasets under a root, and --json-out retains the report. Open-loop action replay Restore an episode's first frame and execute its recorded actions in a fresh environment. The release criterion is success reached at any step, not exact trajectory identity. python -m data_gen.replay.replay_success_rate --jobs 3 --json-out replay.json \ data/sharpa/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 The supplied OpenCabinet release-validation run reported: n=100 ever-success 100/100 (100%) final-success 98/100 (98%) ever-success counts episodes that reach the predicate; final-success counts those still successful at the last step. A trajectory can drift yet reach success. !! INCOMPLETE means a worker failed and the rate was withheld; rerun rather than score only surviving episodes. Inspect an episode and check labels Render the replay alongside the recording with contact and drift summaries: python -m data_gen.replay.batch_compare --episodes 1 --out replay_compare \ data/sharpa/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 The output includes side-by-side videos and summary.csv . After changing a task's evaluate() , recheck labels on restored frames: python -m data_gen.replay.check_label_parity --episodes 3 \ data/sharpa/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 How the release subset is selected build_replay_success_subset selects the 100 replay-successful episodes with the shortest time to success per task and re-exports them through the certified path. The default is a selection preview; --apply performs the export. Do not use it to overwrite an original release dataset. python -m data_gen.replay.build_replay_success_subset --replay-json replay.json \ --source-root data --only CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 Rendering state-only data Supplementary data_append/ datasets do not have videos. Multi-view renderer ↗ restores each frame and writes the family rig: one fixed camera and one wrist camera per active arm, at 256 × 256. State columns are copied without simulating the demonstration forward. Image-policy trainers use Pixel-demo renderer ↗ to produce HDF5 inputs with the training camera contract. Follow Training · render demonstrations rather than assuming every preview camera is a policy input. References: Review/export ↗ , Replay tools ↗ , Offline rendering ↗ . ← Previous Policy integration Next → Collection background

title: Tutorial: from data to evaluation — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Tutorial: from data to evaluation Tutorial: from data to evaluation Follow OpenCabinet from a fresh checkout to replay checks, image inputs, training and a reproducible checkpoint evaluation. One stage, the whole pipeline This walkthrough uses OpenCabinet , the first stage of Cabinet & Pouring: CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 , the left Franka arm with a Sharpa hand, a registered 600-step horizon and 100 released demonstration episodes. It is one stage, not the complete cabinet sequence. Install the public runtime and meshes Download and validate a stage dataset Render fixed policy inputs Train ACT or choose a released checkpoint Evaluate, preserve episode records and compare the declared protocol Keep functional checks separate from benchmark results Short runs and the maintainers' November release-validation observations help check an installation. They do not update the manuscript Leaderboard. The public code has evolved since the paper; report the exact source, checkpoint and evaluation settings. 1. Install and authenticate Follow Installation , including the RTX 50-series wheel adjustment if needed. Request access on the dataset page ↗ before running: git clone https://github.com/SIPAIR-Elastic/DexArena.git cd DexArena conda create -n ms3 python=3.10 conda activate ms3 python -m pip install datasets "lerobot==0.4.0" python -m pip install --upgrade mani_skill "gymnasium==0.29.1" tyro swanlab h5py tensorboard coacd hf auth login hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --include "assets/**" --local-dir tasks python -m pip install pytest python -m pytest tests -q 2. Get the data and resolve task metadata Keep the following shell variables in the same terminal for the later steps: DEX_ENV=CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 DEX_ROBOT=panda_sharpa_hand_left_angled_mobile_base hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --include "data/sharpa/$DEX_ENV/**" --local-dir . python -c "from utils.dex_tasks import resolve_dex_task; t=resolve_dex_task('$DEX_ENV'); print(t.robot_uids, t.max_episode_steps)" Inspect the downloaded Parquet files in Python. Shell variables are not Python local variables, so define the task name explicitly: from pathlib import Path import pandas as pd env_id = "CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1" files = sorted(Path("data/sharpa", env_id, "data/chunk-000").glob("*.parquet")) df = pd.concat((pd.read_parquet(path) for path in files), ignore_index=True) print(len(df), df["episode_index"].nunique()) # release snapshot: 13121, 100 3. Check restoration and replay python -m data_gen.replay.verify_recording_fidelity --episodes 2 --action-replay data/sharpa/$DEX_ENV python -m data_gen.replay.replay_success_rate --jobs 3 --json-out replay.json data/sharpa/$DEX_ENV Look for a faithful restoration result and a complete replay denominator. The maintainers' reference run reached success on 100/100 episodes; 98/100 remained successful at the final step. Your report should retain its own output and source fingerprint. See the two validation contracts . 4. Render image-policy inputs python -m data_gen.render_pixel_demos --demo-path data/sharpa/$DEX_ENV --env-id $DEX_ENV \ --robot-uids $DEX_ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 --max-episode-steps 600 \ --out data/pixels/"$DEX_ENV"_256.h5 python train/prepare_image_dataset.py --pixels data/pixels/"$DEX_ENV"_256.h5 --out data/act/$DEX_ENV The converted dataset contains state/action arrays, six image arrays (two cameras × history offsets 0, 2, 4), episode metadata and dataset_info.json . Inspect the renderer's first episode before training. This reconstructs recorded frames; it is not a new simulation rollout. 5. Train ACT This copyable example defines its camera and environment flags on the page. It runs 20,000 updates on the released stage data; GPU time and memory depend on your machine. Bash arrays keep every flag separate. DEX_CAMS=( --camera-names base_camera_t0 base_camera_tm2 base_camera_tm4 task_wrist_camera_t0 task_wrist_camera_tm2 task_wrist_camera_tm4 --camera-map base_camera_t0=base_camera base_camera_tm2=base_camera base_camera_tm4=base_camera task_wrist_camera_t0=task_wrist_camera task_wrist_camera_tm2=task_wrist_camera task_wrist_camera_tm4=task_wrist_camera --camera-history-offsets base_camera_t0=0 base_camera_tm2=2 base_camera_tm4=4 task_wrist_camera_t0=0 task_wrist_camera_tm2=2 task_wrist_camera_tm4=4 ) DEX_ENVFLAGS=( --env-id "$DEX_ENV" --task-module tasks --robot-uids "$DEX_ROBOT" --control-mode pd_joint_pos --obs-mode rgb --env-kwarg show_guidance_markers=false --sim-backend physx_cpu --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 --policy-state-mode paths --online-state-paths agent.qpos --expected-raw-state-dim 29 --expected-policy-state-dim 29 ) python train/train_ACT.py --demo-data-path data/act/$DEX_ENV "${DEX_ENVFLAGS[@]}" "${DEX_CAMS[@]}" \ --validation-ratio 0.1 --image-mean 0.485 0.456 0.406 --image-std 0.229 0.224 0.225 \ --image-encoder-backbone resnet18 --image-encoder-pretrained --chunk-size 25 --prior-l1-weight 1.0 \ --action-loss-groups 0:7 7:29 --action-loss-group-weights 2.0 1.0 \ --batch-size 16 --num-workers 4 --steps 20000 --eval-every 1000 --save-every 1000 --num-eval-episodes 0 \ --output-dir runs/act --exp-name "$DEX_ENV"_s1 --seed 1 For Diffusion Policy, PPO, RLPD, GR00T or π0.5, use the method-specific recipes and runtimes in Training . The tutorial does not start a long-running training process for you. 6. Evaluate a released checkpoint You can skip training and evaluate the released ACT policy. This example uses the registered 600-step horizon and 50 episodes; it is not the draft's shorter 400-step functional recipe. Resolve the horizon again if you switch tasks. hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --local-dir . --include "ckpt/act/$DEX_ENV/**" python train/train_ACT.py --evaluate --checkpoint ckpt/act/$DEX_ENV/ckpt.pt \ --env-id $DEX_ENV --task-module tasks --robot-uids $DEX_ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \ --obs-mode rgb --env-kwarg show_guidance_markers=false --sim-backend physx_cpu \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 \ --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 600 --eval-seed 1 --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 \ --capture-video --max-eval-videos 3 Inspect the per-episode [EVAL] lines, final JSON summary, videos and the CSV under ckpt/act/$DEX_ENV/eval_logs_eval_only/ . To test your training run, replace --checkpoint with a checkpoint file under runs/act/ . 7. Read and report the result One task's success rate is not the method's benchmark average. Stage execution averages the 30 stage rates; cross-scene evaluation repeats a frozen policy on the three named kitchens; long-horizon evaluation attempts all stages of a complete sequence after one reset. The released ACT manifest reports 47/50 on OpenCabinet. That is a checkpoint-release record, not a promise that a changed code revision, seed list or horizon will reproduce the same count. The manuscript scores on the Leaderboard remain a distinct fixed snapshot. Follow what to report with a number : code and data revisions, checkpoint hash, environment, embodiment, camera preprocessing, horizon, seeds, instruction rule, scene and per-episode records. 8. Continue the experiment Another task: resolve its robot, horizon and inputs using Task metadata ↗ and the task table ↗ . Another hand: inspect -Wuji-v1 , -XHand-v1 and -Gripper-v1 ; published demonstrations and checkpoints are Sharpa-only. Scene transfer or complete sequences: follow Evaluation and Long-horizon guide ↗ . Sharing a result: preserve reproduction artifacts and include the citation . ← Previous Installation Next → Resources & release status
