title: Training — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Training Training Prepare policy observations, train the six benchmark baselines, and preserve a reproducible experiment contract. The shared training contract Start with Installation and download the task-matched released demonstrations . The six benchmark methods use the Sharpa hand; the public task registry additionally supports other end effectors. Choose the environment from the official task table ↗ rather than inheriting an unrelated trainer default. Contract Required setting Task identity <Task>-<Hand>-v1 . Pass the exact environment ID and its registered robot. OpenCabinet uses CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 and panda_sharpa_hand_left_angled_mobile_base . Control and actions pd_joint_pos : absolute joint targets in radians; 29 channels for one arm and Sharpa hand, 58 for both. Match joint ordering and the selected trainer’s action parameterization. Reward Task environments expose sparse (the success indicator) and none ; trainers default to sparse . Dataset data/sharpa/<environment ID> . Render policy images from the recorded simulator states before image-based training. Camera contract Fixed scene camera plus the task’s wrist camera(s). Use cabinet_fixed for pixel/ACT/DP preparation and robodex_fixed for VLA preparation; keep names, resolution and history consistent with the chosen loader. Storage roots Relative data paths resolve against $ROBODEX_DATA_ROOT ; checkpoints and runs use $ROBODEX_STORAGE_ROOT / $ROBODEX_RUNS_ROOT . The repository is the default root. Trainer arguments are defined in train/train_configs/ ↗ . Run python train/<trainer>.py --help to inspect its exact CLI. Most trainers accept hyphenated flags; the GR00T examples retain their documented underscore spelling. Recipe horizons are not a new evaluation protocol The examples below preserve the released OpenCabinet training recipes, including their separate 400-, 500- and 600-step settings. A rendering limit or an in-training rollout setting does not redefine the registered benchmark horizon. For a final score, resolve the canonical task settings and use the Evaluation guide . The six baselines Method Entry point Policy input Data preparation PPO train_ppo_pixels.py ↗ Two 128 × 128 cameras + proprioception Rendered HDF5 for the BC anchor; LeRobot recordings for demo-state resets. RLPD train_rlpd_pixels.py ↗ Two 128 × 128 cameras + proprioception Rendered HDF5. ACT train_ACT.py ↗ 256 × 256 camera history at offsets 0, 2 and 4 + joint positions Rendered HDF5, then prepare_image_dataset.py. Diffusion Policy train_DP.py ↗ Same observation contract as ACT Same image/history preparation as ACT. GR00T N1.7 train_groot.py ↗ Fixed 256 × 256 rig + task instruction VLA render → LeRobot v2.1 conversion → modality configuration. π0.5 train_pi05.py ↗ Fixed 256 × 256 rig + task instruction Episode-labelled LeRobot v3.0 data, robot/controller binding and data contract. The commands use OpenCabinet. To train another stage, replace ENV , its robot, task-specific observation dimensions and recipe limits together. Query utils.dex_tasks.resolve_dex_task(env_id).robot_uids instead of reusing the OpenCabinet robot for every task. Full guides: image and state baseline guide ↗ , GR00T guide ↗ , and π0.5 guide ↗ . Step 1 · Render the demonstrations Policy-camera preparation restores every stored simulator frame and re-renders the fixed rig; it does not simulate the recorded actions forward. Released multi-view videos are useful for inspection, but the trainers below require their specified image/state export. The HDF5 contains the policy cameras and proprioception at each control step. ENV=CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 ROBOT=panda_sharpa_hand_left_angled_mobile_base # PPO / RLPD: 128x128 python -m data_gen.render_pixel_demos --demo-path data/sharpa/$ENV --env-id $ENV \ --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos --sim-backend physx_cuda \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 128 --max-episode-steps 500 \ --save-video --out data/pixels/${ENV}_128.h5 # ACT / DP: 256x256, then materialise the history offsets python -m data_gen.render_pixel_demos --demo-path data/sharpa/$ENV --env-id $ENV \ --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 --max-episode-steps 600 \ --out data/pixels/${ENV}_256.h5 python train/prepare_image_dataset.py --pixels data/pixels/${ENV}_256.h5 --out data/act/$ENV Use --limit N for a small preparation trial. Tasks whose stored frames toggle a render body’s visibility, such as CabinetPouringPickBottle-Sharpa-v1 , need --sim-backend physx_cpu . --save-video writes both camera views of episode 0 side by side; inspect it before training. The image preparation script prints the --camera-names , --camera-map and --camera-history-offsets flags that match its output arrays. Pixel demonstration renderer ↗ · Image/history dataset preparation ↗ Step 2 · Train a policy ACT ACT decodes a 25-step action chunk through a conditional VAE and evaluates with temporal ensembling. The released ACT runs use 12,000–20,000 updates on the 100 released episodes of each stage. Diffusion Policy DP generates a 16-step chunk with a temporal U-Net and 100 DDPM steps, then executes receding-horizon actions. Its released runs use 20,000 updates, batch 16. Shared image-policy preparation and commands These OpenCabinet commands select 20,000 updates and explicitly bind the camera history and 29-dimensional joint-position state. Keep camera order, normalization, state paths and action dimensions with each checkpoint. CAMS="--camera-names base_camera_t0 base_camera_tm2 base_camera_tm4 task_wrist_camera_t0 task_wrist_camera_tm2 task_wrist_camera_tm4 \ --camera-map base_camera_t0=base_camera base_camera_tm2=base_camera base_camera_tm4=base_camera task_wrist_camera_t0=task_wrist_camera task_wrist_camera_tm2=task_wrist_camera task_wrist_camera_tm4=task_wrist_camera \ --camera-history-offsets base_camera_t0=0 base_camera_tm2=2 base_camera_tm4=4 task_wrist_camera_t0=0 task_wrist_camera_tm2=2 task_wrist_camera_tm4=4" ENVFLAGS="--env-id $ENV --task-module tasks --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \ --obs-mode rgb --env-kwarg show_guidance_markers=false --sim-backend physx_cpu --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 \ --policy-state-mode paths --online-state-paths agent.qpos --expected-raw-state-dim 29 --expected-policy-state-dim 29" python train/train_ACT.py --demo-data-path data/act/$ENV $ENVFLAGS $CAMS \ --validation-ratio 0.1 --image-mean 0.485 0.456 0.406 --image-std 0.229 0.224 0.225 \ --image-encoder-backbone resnet18 --image-encoder-pretrained --chunk-size 25 --prior-l1-weight 1.0 \ --action-loss-groups 0:7 7:29 --action-loss-group-weights 2.0 1.0 \ --batch-size 16 --num-workers 4 --steps 20000 --eval-every 1000 --save-every 1000 --num-eval-episodes 0 \ --output-dir runs/act --exp-name ${ENV}_s1 --seed 1 python train/train_DP.py --demo-data-path data/act/$ENV $ENVFLAGS $CAMS --no-filter-success \ --batch-size 16 --num-workers 4 --steps 20000 --eval-every 1000 --save-every 1000 --num-eval-episodes 0 \ --check-env-before-training --output-dir runs/dp --exp-name ${ENV}_s1 --seed 1 The examples disable online evaluation during training with --num-eval-episodes 0 ; use the separate frozen-checkpoint evaluation afterward. ACT and image Diffusion Policy training ↗ RLPD from pixels RLPD mixes demonstration and online samples symmetrically. Its LayerNorm critic ensemble uses a random-subset minimum target; only the critic loss trains the visual encoder. This is the released configuration shared across the 30 stage tasks, with task-specific episode limits. python train/train_rlpd_pixels.py \ --env-id $ENV --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \ --demo-data-path data/pixels/${ENV}_128.h5 \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 128 \ --reward-mode sparse --reward-bias -1 \ --delta-action --delta-action-scale 0.2 \ --encoder-arch d4pg --latent-dim-per-cam 64 \ --encoder-grad-source critic_only --augmentation --augment-pad 4 \ --max-episode-steps 600 --num-eval-steps 600 \ --num-envs 1 --utd-ratio 1 --num-qs 5 --num-min-qs 2 --gamma 0.999 \ --batch-size 256 --buffer-size 200000 --start-steps 5000 \ --total-env-steps 600000 --eval-freq 20000 --save-freq 20000 \ --num-eval-envs 1 --num-eval-episodes 20 --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 \ --exp-name ${ENV}_rlpd_pixels --track --delta-action enables residual joint-position control: a normalized action becomes a_t = clip(a_(t−1) + u × scale) , and demonstrations are transformed into that same parameterization at load time. --reward-bias -1 changes the binary success reward into a per-step cost. A 200,000-transition replay buffer with two 128 × 128 cameras requires approximately 19 GiB of host RAM. PPO from pixels Online PPO uses the same visual observation, with demonstrations anchoring it twice: a BC loss on the rendered HDF5, including a pure-BC warm-up, and demonstration-state resets from the LeRobot dataset under a reverse curriculum. Its 64 collection environments require GPU physics. python train/train_ppo_pixels.py \ --env-id $ENV --robot-uids $ROBOT \ --control-mode pd_joint_pos --reward-mode sparse \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 128 \ --max-episode-steps 400 \ --num-envs 64 --num-steps 200 --num-minibatches 32 --update-epochs 1 \ --total-timesteps 5000000 --stop-at-step 1000000 \ --learning-rate 3e-4 --actor-learning-rate 3e-5 \ --gamma 0.99 --gae-lambda 0.95 --clip-coef 0.2 \ --target-kl 0.2 --kl-stop-scope policy --recompute-old-logprob \ --ent-coef 0.0 --vf-coef 0.5 --max-grad-norm 0.5 --actor-logstd-init -3.5 \ --action-scale-source demos --action-scale-margin 0.1 \ --hidden-dims 512 512 512 512 \ --encoder-arch d4pg --latent-dim-per-cam 128 \ --encoder-sharing separate_per_head --encoder-grad-source actor_and_critic \ --augmentation --augment-pad 4 \ --use-bc-loss --bc-data-path data/pixels/${ENV}_128.h5 \ --bc-coef 1.0 --bc-min-coef 0.05 --bc-decay-steps 0.5 \ --bc-batch-size 256 --bc-loss-type mse --bc-val-fraction 0.1 \ --bc-warmup-steps 20000 --bc-warmup-batch-size 256 \ --use-demo-init-states \ --demo-init-data-path data/sharpa/$ENV \ --demo-init-prob 1.0 --demo-init-min-prob 0.1 --demo-init-decay-steps 0.7 \ --demo-init-curriculum progress \ --demo-init-curriculum-start-frac 0.2 --demo-init-curriculum-steps 0.5 \ --demo-init-advance-success 0.5 --demo-init-success-window 200 \ --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 \ --num-eval-envs 25 --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 400 \ --eval-freq 100000 --save-freq 200000 \ --exp-name ${ENV}_ppo_pixels --track --stop-at-step 1000000 ends collection at one million environment steps while all schedules retain the --total-timesteps 5000000 clock. Do not change one budget flag without reviewing the dependent warm-up, regularization and curriculum schedules. GR00T N1.7 Use the GR00T runtime Build the dedicated runtime with bash scripts/groot/setup_env.sh , then run these commands with libs/Isaac-GR00T/.venv/bin/python as python . Dataset conversion needs FFmpeg and the libraries used by torchcodec. Accept the Hub terms for nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2-2B before loading its gated backbone. See model runtimes and the upstream GR00T guide. DEX_OUT holds datasets/ , runs/ and evals/ . The renderer assigns one of the task’s four registered instructions to each episode, with 25 episodes per phrasing. It restores the fixed 256 × 256 rig and writes controller-ordered joint vectors. export DEX_OUT="$PWD/outputs/groot" STEM=$(python -c "from utils.dex_tasks import resolve_dex_task as r; print(r('$ENV').short_name)") DS=$DEX_OUT/datasets/${STEM}_rig_vla python utils/groot_utils/replay_to_vla_dataset.py \ --src data/sharpa/${ENV} --dst "$DS" --env_id $ENV --control_mode pd_joint_pos \ --proprio controller_qpos --camera_size 256 --camera_profile robodex_fixed --verify_frames 6 \ --gpu_id 0 --overwrite python libs/Isaac-GR00T/scripts/lerobot_conversion/convert_v3_to_v2.py --root $DEX_OUT/datasets --repo-id ${STEM}_rig_vla python utils/groot_utils/modality_configs.py --env-id $ENV --write-json "$DS" python scripts/groot/validate_dataset.py --dataset-path "$DS" --env-id $ENV The converter changes the dataset at $DS to LeRobot v2.1 for GR00T and preserves its original v3.0 copy at <dataset name>_v3.0 . Keep that copy for π0.5. --overwrite rebuilds the selected generated dataset; choose a new output path if an existing export must be retained. Rendering and conversion details ↗ Full-parameter fine-tuning of GR00T N1.7-3B unfreezes vision and language backbones: effective batch 32, learning rate 4 × 10 −5 , 12,000 updates, one 80 GB GPU, approximately 64 GB used. The action-head-only option --no_tune_llm --no_tune_visual uses approximately 20 GB, but is a different training setting. Replace the local model placeholder with your downloaded nvidia/GR00T-N1.7-3B directory. python train/train_groot.py \ --dataset_path "$DS" --env_id $ENV --base_model_path /path/to/GR00T-N1.7-3B \ --modality_config_path utils/groot_utils/modality_configs.py \ --output_dir $DEX_OUT/runs/groot_${STEM}_rig --num_gpus 1 --master_port 29500 \ --global_batch_size 2 --gradient_accumulation_steps 16 --learning_rate 4e-05 \ --max_steps 12000 --save_steps 1000 --save_total_limit 2 Checkpoints are written every --save_steps ; the final directory is checkpoint-12000 . Use --resume_from_checkpoint 1 with the same output directory to restore the newest checkpoint and training state. The long-horizon guide ↗ merges each complete task’s stage datasets with utils/groot_utils/merge_family_dataset.py and trains one family checkpoint with the same budget. Keep instruction protocols explicit The public multi-instruction GR00T release uses per-episode registered phrasings. Its checkpoint results are not interchangeable with the manuscript’s single-instruction setting. Preserve the dataset labels and declare the evaluation instruction rule; the website leaderboard remains the manuscript baseline record. π0.5 Prepare three task-specific inputs: the robot/controller binding from the registered environment, a data contract recording camera shapes, channel names and normalization, and a file manifest of the original π0.5 Base. Data preparation runs in the simulator environment; LoRA training runs in the separate Python 3.11 OpenPI environment described in the installation guide ↗ . # After GR00T conversion, select the preserved LeRobot v3.0 copy. DS=$DEX_OUT/datasets/${STEM}_rig_vla_v3.0 mkdir -p prep python -m utils.pi05_utils.binding --env-id $ENV --output prep/${ENV}-binding.json python -m utils.pi05_utils.data --dataset-root "$DS" --binding prep/${ENV}-binding.json \ --env-id $ENV --output prep/${ENV}-data.json python -m utils.pi05_utils.base_manifest --base /path/to/pi05_base --output prep/pi05_base-manifest.json /path/to/pi05-venv/bin/python train/train_pi05.py \ --dataset-path "$DS" \ --data-contract prep/${ENV}-data.json \ --binding prep/${ENV}-binding.json \ --base-model-path /path/to/pi05_base \ --base-manifest prep/pi05_base-manifest.json \ --output-dir runs/${ENV}-lora This example follows GR00T preparation and explicitly selects its preserved v3.0 export. If you render directly for π0.5 without converting for GR00T, set DS to that original episode-labelled LeRobot v3.0 output instead. The Base directory contains params/ (approximately 12.4 GB) from the public gs://openpi-assets/checkpoints/pi05_base bucket; use the download recipe in Evaluation . π0.5 setting Value Backbone / expert gemma_2b_lora / gemma_300m_lora Single-arm / dual-arm updates 30,000 / 60,000 Global batch / action horizon 32 / 30 Resume --resume restores the latest complete training checkpoint, optimizer and RNG state. Use train/train_pi05.py for both fine-tuning and --evaluate . The current fine-tuning guide ↗ defines the exact model/runtime pins and checkpoint contract. Released inference-only overlays are not optimizer/RNG checkpoints and cannot be used as training-resume state. Additional state-based agents The public training guide ↗ also documents state BC, FQE/SARSA, AWR, CQL, IQL, TD3+BC, OPT, SAC, RLPD, Diffusion BC and DPPO. They read the LeRobot state dataset directly, without pixel rendering. For example: python train/train_iql.py \ --env_id CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 --control_mode pd_joint_pos \ --demo_data_path data/sharpa/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 --success_only \ --iql_expectile 0.7 --iql_beta 3.0 --bc_warmup_steps 20000 --actor_bc_weight 1.0 \ --total_updates 500000 --exp_name opencabinet_iql --track These additional agents are not extra manuscript baselines. Most trainers expose SwanLab/TensorBoard tracking controls such as --track / --no-track and write under runs/ . π0.5 instead preserves its own durable metrics, run metadata and per-seed records; do not assume identical logging flags across every trainer. Original method references These primary publications and official projects describe the original algorithms. The commands above document DexArena-specific observation, data and control choices. PPO · Original paper ↗ RLPD · ICML 2023 paper ↗ ACT · Original ALOHA / ACT project ↗ Diffusion Policy · Original project & paper ↗ GR00T N1.7 · Official NVIDIA repository ↗ π0.5 · Official Physical Intelligence report ↗ Freeze, evaluate and report Keep the source revision, dataset identity, preprocessing outputs, episode split, seed and complete resolved configuration with the checkpoint. Declare a checkpoint-selection rule without using held-out evaluation scenes for tuning. Freeze the checkpoint and camera/action adapters before scoring the canonical task, native scenes or complete sequences. Record episode-level outcomes and aggregate using the benchmark score protocol , not the best training rollout. Continue to Evaluation for released checkpoints and exact result artifacts, follow the end-to-end tutorial for a single task, or browse source and release references . ← Previous Collection background Next → Evaluation

title: Evaluation — DexArena Docs
text:
Docs / Evaluation Evaluation Evaluate all six released baselines, preserve the task and camera contract, and distinguish release validation from benchmark results. Keep the evaluation contract fixed Choose a registered task, freeze a checkpoint, and retain the complete episode records. The benchmark measures physical success, not the similarity of a rollout to a demonstration. Finish the installation checks and download the required assets and data before running these commands from the repository root. Track Evaluation unit Success and aggregation Stage execution 30 stage tasks, 50 episodes per stage Evaluate each stage from its own reset distribution at its registered horizon. Average stage success rates with equal task weights. Cross-scene generalization 30 stages × 3 native kitchen scenes Reuse the frozen policy across scenes. Average the stages within each scene first, then report the mean and standard deviation of the three scene averages. Long-horizon composition 10 complete tasks, 50 episodes per task Reset once per episode; execute stages in order without resetting the scene. Success requires the final stage within the complete task’s horizon. Success, horizons and seeds Success: the task’s physical success predicate must become true at some step. The ACT, DP, PPO and RLPD evaluators expose eval_success_once_mean ; GR00T and π0.5 report a success rate in summary.json . Persistent hold and latch conditions remain part of the predicate. Control: preserve pd_joint_pos absolute targets and the 20 Hz control rate. Query resolve_dex_task(env_id).max_episode_steps rather than copying another task’s time limit. Seeds: the release-validation recipes below use seed 1 for ACT, DP, PPO and RLPD; GR00T and π0.5 use environment seeds 10001–10050. These recipes do not establish identical manuscript seed ranges: the manuscript records ACT/DP stage seeds 50000–50049. Record the actual episode-seed manifest and consult the score protocol before comparing results. Cameras are part of the checkpoint Use the fixed scene and wrist camera rig: 256 × 256 images for ACT, DP, GR00T and π0.5, and 128 × 128 for the released PPO/RLPD pixel checkpoints. The relevant flags are --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size <px> or GR00T’s --camera_profile robodex_fixed . The task’s default base_camera is a different view, not an interchangeable input. Preserve camera order, history offsets, image normalization and state layout. Release validation is not the leaderboard The command recipes and small-run observations on this page come from the supplied release-validation notes, prepared on 9 November 2026 against code revision c284d4d on one RTX 5090 workstation. They check released artifacts and execution paths; they do not replace the frozen manuscript results on the Leaderboard . In particular, three- or fifteen-episode checks are not benchmark scores. Download a released checkpoint Checkpoints are hosted under ckpt/ in SIPAIR/DexArena ↗ . Request access to the gated dataset repository and run hf auth login once. Select only the directories you need; the complete collection is substantially larger than one task. hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --local-dir . \ --include "ckpt/<method>/<directory>/**" Path on the Hub Release identity Count and approximate size ckpt/act/<env id>/{ckpt.pt,config.json} ACT paper checkpoints. ckpt/manifest.json records the environment ID and a 50-episode score for each checkpoint. 30 checkpoints · 6.4 GB ckpt/dp/<env id>/{ckpt.pt,config.json} Diffusion Policy paper checkpoints. The manifest records the 10-episode checkpoint-selection score; it is not a new 50-episode benchmark run. 30 checkpoints · 41 GB ckpt/ppo/<env id>/ckpt.pt PPO-from-pixels checkpoint for each stage task. 30 checkpoints · 3.6 GB ckpt/rlpd/<env id>/ckpt.pt RLPD-from-pixels checkpoint for each stage task. 30 checkpoints · 1.4 GB ckpt/gr00t-n1.7-multi-instruction/<Task>/ ckpt/gr00t-n1.7-multi-instruction/long-horizon/<Task>/ GR00T N1.7 release checkpoints trained with per-episode instruction sampling: one of four registered phrasings. These are not the manuscript’s single-instruction checkpoints. The manuscript checkpoints are not published. See the multi-instruction results column in the GR00T guide. 30 stage + 10 complete-task checkpoints · 503 GB, about 12.6 GB each ckpt/pi05/<trained env id>/ π0.5 paper packages: inference-only overlays containing the trainable arrays, to be loaded on the verified public π0.5 Base. Legacy directory IDs remain; read config.json for the task mapping. 30 stage + long-horizon packages · 112 GB For example, π0.5’s CabinetPourDoorOpen-v1 package maps to the current CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 environment. Do not rename a package or infer a binding from the directory name alone. The resources page links the checkpoint inventory and method guides. Resolve the registered robot and horizon The examples use OpenCabinet, whose registered horizon is 600 control steps . Run this in the simulator environment before adapting a command to another task. The complete task list is in the Task registry ↗ . ENV=CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 read H ROBOT < <(python -c "from utils.dex_tasks import resolve_dex_task as r; t=r('$ENV'); print(t.max_episode_steps, t.robot_uids)") printf 'Environment: %s
Horizon: %s
Robot: %s
' "$ENV" "$H" "$ROBOT" Checkpoint recipes and canonical horizons are different The supplied release recipes below use 400 steps for ACT/PPO , 500 for RLPD , and 600 for DP on OpenCabinet. They are reproduced as identifiable checkpoint-validation recipes, not presented as canonical full-horizon leaderboard runs. For a registered-horizon evaluation, substitute --num-eval-steps "$H" for ACT/DP, and --num-eval-steps "$H" --max-episode-steps "$H" for PPO/RLPD, using the resolver above. On this task H=600 . Record that change, use the required seed manifest, and rerun all planned episodes under the score protocol ; do not attach the short-recipe observations to the changed run. ACT and Diffusion Policy Run in the main conda environment. The evaluator restores camera names, temporal offsets, image normalization and state layout from the checkpoint. The fixed camera flags below install the views on which the checkpoint was trained. These are the supplied release-validation recipes; apply the registered-horizon correction before a canonical comparison. hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --local-dir . \ --include "ckpt/act/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1/**" "ckpt/dp/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1/**" # ACT release recipe: temporal ensembling; a new chunk every control step. # The recipe's 400-step limit is shorter than this task's 600-step horizon. python train/train_ACT.py --evaluate --checkpoint ckpt/act/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1/ckpt.pt \ --env-id CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 --task-module tasks \ --robot-uids panda_sharpa_hand_left_angled_mobile_base --control-mode pd_joint_pos \ --obs-mode rgb --env-kwarg show_guidance_markers=false --sim-backend physx_cpu \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 \ --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 400 --eval-seed 1 --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 # DP release recipe: execute 16 actions from each predicted chunk. python train/train_DP.py --evaluate --checkpoint ckpt/dp/CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1/ckpt.pt \ --env-id CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 --task-module tasks \ --robot-uids panda_sharpa_hand_left_angled_mobile_base --control-mode pd_joint_pos \ --obs-mode rgb --env-kwarg show_guidance_markers=false --sim-backend physx_cpu \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 --action-chunk-size 16 \ --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 600 --eval-seed 1 --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 Read the logs and inspect a rollout Each episode prints an [EVAL] line containing return, length and success_once ; the run ends with a JSON summary. Per-episode CSV files are written under <checkpoint directory>/eval_logs_eval_only/ . Add --capture-video --max-eval-videos N to save renders of the first N episodes beside the checkpoint. DP execution chunk size changes the experiment --action-chunk-size is the number of generated actions actually executed before the next policy query; its default is 4. The supplied OpenCabinet validation notes report 11/15 successes with 16 actions and 3/15 with the default 4 over the same seeds. These are small functional checks, not leaderboard results. Always report the value alongside a DP score. ACT’s supplied short validation passed 3/3 episodes; its release manifest records 47/50. Keep the manifest entry, the recipe’s episode cap, and any newly measured result separate. Source: training and evaluation guide ↗ . PPO and RLPD from pixels Use the main conda environment and the same camera and encoder settings as training. Both pixel checkpoints carry a camera-configuration hash and reject incompatible camera settings. Both also need a small rendered demonstration file: RLPD uses the first action when applying --delta-action , while PPO derives its action scale from the demonstrations. Five rendered episodes suffice for this input. Render the small auxiliary input The 500-step value below belongs to the supplied auxiliary-render recipe; it is not an instruction to shorten the registered evaluation horizon. See Data & replay for dataset integrity and Training for the full image-data preparation workflow. ENV=CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 ROBOT=panda_sharpa_hand_left_angled_mobile_base python -m data_gen.render_pixel_demos --demo-path data/sharpa/$ENV --env-id $ENV --robot-uids $ROBOT \ --control-mode pd_joint_pos --sim-backend physx_cuda --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 128 \ --max-episode-steps 500 --limit 5 --out data/pixels/"$ENV"_5_128.h5 hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --local-dir . --include "ckpt/rlpd/$ENV/**" "ckpt/ppo/$ENV/**" Evaluate RLPD # Supplied release recipe: 50 episodes in one environment, 500-step cap. # Use registry-derived H for both step flags in a canonical full-horizon run. python train/train_rlpd_pixels.py --evaluate --checkpoint ckpt/rlpd/$ENV/ckpt.pt \ --env-id $ENV --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 128 --encoder-arch d4pg --num-qs 5 \ --delta-action --delta-action-scale 0.2 --normalize-proprio \ --demo-data-path data/pixels/"$ENV"_5_128.h5 \ --seed 1 --num-eval-envs 1 --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 500 --max-episode-steps 500 \ --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 --no-track --exp-name "$ENV"_rlpd_eval Evaluate PPO # Supplied release recipe: 50 environments × one episode, 400-step cap. # Use registry-derived H for both step flags in a canonical full-horizon run. python train/train_ppo_pixels.py --evaluate --checkpoint ckpt/ppo/$ENV/ckpt.pt \ --env-id $ENV --robot-uids $ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \ --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 128 --encoder-arch d4pg --latent-dim-per-cam 128 --normalize-proprio \ --action-scale-source demos --bc-data-path data/pixels/"$ENV"_5_128.h5 \ --bc-warmup-steps 0 --no-use-demo-init-states \ --seed 1 --num-eval-envs 50 --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 400 --max-episode-steps 400 \ --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 --no-track --exp-name "$ENV"_ppo_eval Both evaluators print eval_success_once_mean . The supplied three-episode functional checks produced RLPD 3/3 and PPO 1/3 on OpenCabinet; neither value is a new benchmark estimate. --capture-video adds a diagnostic render camera without replacing the policy cameras. For a native kitchen background, add --scene-background <scene id> and use --sim-backend physx_cpu . Also change PPO’s --num-eval-envs 50 to --num-eval-envs 1 : native-scene evaluation is serial, not the 50-environment recipe above. Preserve the registered horizon and see Cross-scene evaluation . GR00T N1.7 Run the evaluator with the GR00T interpreter described in Installation . The required backbone, nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2-2B , is gated separately from the DexArena dataset: accept its terms and authenticate, or point GROOT_BACKBONE_PATH to a local copy. The path must contain nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2 ; the loader records it in the checkpoint’s config.json , so keep a consistent local path for each checkpoint. Published multi-instruction models are not the manuscript checkpoints The public gr00t-n1.7-multi-instruction models use one of four registered phrasings per episode. The manuscript scores were obtained with single-instruction models that are not published. Use --instruction_sampling registered for the released models’ documented protocol. Switching to canonical changes inference instructions but does not turn a multi-instruction checkpoint into the unpublished paper checkpoint. See the GR00T checkpoint and results guide ↗ . ENV=CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --local-dir . --include "ckpt/gr00t-n1.7-multi-instruction/OpenCabinet/**" hf download nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2-2B --local-dir models/nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2-2B export GROOT_BACKBONE_PATH=$PWD/models/nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2-2B export DEX_OUT=/data/dex read H ROBOT < <(python -c "from utils.dex_tasks import resolve_dex_task as r; t=r('$ENV'); print(t.max_episode_steps, t.robot_uids)") python train/train_groot.py --evaluate --model_path ckpt/gr00t-n1.7-multi-instruction/OpenCabinet \ --env_id $ENV --control_mode pd_joint_pos \ --robot_uids $ROBOT --camera_size 256 --camera_profile robodex_fixed \ --instruction_sampling registered --seed 10001 --num_eval_episodes 50 \ --num_eval_steps $H --max_episode_steps $H --sim_backend physx_cpu --action_horizon 8 \ --capture_video --eval_output_dir $DEX_OUT/evals/groot/OpenCabinet/checkpoint-12000 DEX_OUT is an example output directory; choose a writable location. If using the project’s libs/Isaac-GR00T/.venv , invoke its Python interpreter or activate it before the command. Inspect every episode The output directory contains summary.json with the success rate and resolved protocol, episodes.jsonl with seed, instruction, success, length and video path, and videos/ . The supplied release-validation run reports 17/50 on OpenCabinet; the guide records 12/50 for the same published checkpoint. Treat these as distinct recorded runs rather than substituting either for the manuscript leaderboard. Add --scene_background robocasa_l3_s2 for the native-scene path and repeat with the other two scene IDs. Preserve the checkpoint, seeds and instruction-sampling rule. For composition, see Long-horizon evaluation . π0.5 Launch evaluation from the main conda environment; --policy-python starts the JAX policy worker in the pinned OpenPI environment. A released package is an overlay, not a standalone model: it requires the public π0.5 Base and an environment-derived controller binding. See the π0.5 setup and package guide ↗ for the separate runtime. Download the verified Base checkpoint The Base’s params/ directory contains 29 files, approximately 12.4 GB. Download from the public OpenPI bucket with anonymous HTTPS; the package stores every required file’s size and SHA-256 and rejects an incompatible Base. The snippet below skips same-size files for convenience, while the package loader performs its own integrity verification. import json import os import urllib.parse import urllib.request root = "pi05_base" items = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen( "https://storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1/b/openpi-assets/o?prefix=checkpoints/pi05_base/&fields=items(name,size)&maxResults=500" ))["items"] for item in items: relative = item["name"].removeprefix("checkpoints/pi05_base/") destination = os.path.join(root, relative) os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(destination), exist_ok=True) if os.path.exists(destination) and os.path.getsize(destination) == int(item["size"]): continue url = "https://storage.googleapis.com/openpi-assets/" + urllib.parse.quote(item["name"]) urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, destination) Bind the package to the current environment The binding’s --task list must include the package’s own task name, the task field in its config.json . The OpenCabinet package retains its trained environment ID CabinetPourDoorOpen-v1 ; pass the current registered ID through --env-id rather than changing that package directory. ENV=CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1 hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --local-dir . --include "ckpt/pi05/CabinetPourDoorOpen-v1/**" python -m utils.pi05_utils.binding --env-id $ENV --task dooropen --output prep/opencabinet-binding.json python train/train_pi05.py --evaluate \ --model-path ckpt/pi05/CabinetPourDoorOpen-v1 \ --base-model-path pi05_base \ --binding prep/opencabinet-binding.json --env-id $ENV \ --output-dir evals/pi05/opencabinet \ --policy-python /path/to/pi05-venv/bin/python The frozen policy predicts 30-step chunks. A new request is issued when fewer than 24 actions remain; overlapping targets are blended while physics continues. Do not substitute another chunk-execution scheme without documenting the change. Complete the planned seed set The evaluator uses seeds 10001–10050 and retains every attempt under episodes/ . Infrastructure errors are unscored, not silent task failures or successes; the final rate is reported only after all 50 planned seeds are complete. Use --resume to continue pending seeds. The supplied OpenCabinet validation reports 49/50; the manuscript’s OpenCabinet entry is 98%. That agreement does not turn a release-validation run into the full 30-stage evaluation. For cross-scene evaluation, add --scene-background s1 , s2 or s6 , and use a separate output directory for each scene. The loader packages for complete tasks have an additional limitation described below . Evaluate frozen policies across native scenes Use the three named native backgrounds: robocasa_l3_s1 , robocasa_l3_s2 and robocasa_l3_s6 . Keep the task, checkpoint, controller, registered horizon, cameras, preprocessing and episode seeds fixed. The π0.5 CLI accepts the corresponding short IDs s1 , s2 and s6 . Native-scene evaluation requires one CPU-physics environment with episodes run serially. Do not carry the vectorized PPO recipe into this path. Use --sim-backend physx_cpu and --num-eval-envs 1 where those flags are exposed, or their GR00T underscore spellings. Retain the resolved background and camera manifest in each scene’s output directory. Evaluator Background argument Keep explicit ACT / DP / PPO / RLPD --scene-background robocasa_l3_s2 CPU physics, one evaluation environment, registered horizon and fixed checkpoint camera preset. GR00T --scene_background robocasa_l3_s2 --sim_backend physx_cpu , fixed seeds and --instruction_sampling . π0.5 --scene-background s2 Separate output directories for s1 , s2 and s6 ; complete each 50-seed set. First calculate a success rate for each stage/scene pair, then the equal-weight average over stages within each scene, and finally the mean ± standard deviation across those three scene averages. The ± value describes scene variation; it is not a training-seed confidence interval. See the native-scene guide ↗ and the score protocol . Compose stages without resetting the scene A complete-task episode begins with one reset. Stage transitions must preserve the simulator state; resetting between stage policies changes the experiment into separate skill evaluations. Final-stage success must occur within the registered complete-task horizon. GR00T chain and family modes scripts/dex/eval_long_chain.py supports one checkpoint per stage with --mode chain , or a family checkpoint with switching stage instructions through --mode family . Point --ckpt-root to compatible checkpoints with the layout required by the guide. For example: python scripts/dex/eval_long_chain.py \ --long juice --mode chain --ckpt-root $DEX_OUT/runs \ --episodes 50 --out $DEX_OUT/evals/long/chain/juice The juice family is one of ten complete tasks; it is not the entire long-horizon track. Published GR00T family checkpoints still follow the release’s multi-instruction protocol, not the unpublished manuscript checkpoint identity. Follow the complete-task and checkpoint-layout instructions in the GR00T guide ↗ . π0.5 package support and current limit A package loader is not a long-horizon command-line runner The published ckpt/pi05/long-horizon/ packages contain ordered stage policies and a loader. Their stage-switching logic is not yet exposed as a command-line evaluator. The stage command on this page cannot be presented as a complete-task reproduction command. An integration must select the next stage policy from the task’s stage-success signals, keep one continuous scene state, and retain a stage-transition trace. For your own checkpoints, document how policy history and queued chunk actions are handled at every transition. Start with the single-task tutorial and training guide , then retain full episode evidence before aggregating complete-task results. Report an identifiable experiment A success percentage is meaningful only with its evaluation contract. Store the per-episode CSV or episodes.jsonl from which it was calculated and keep initialization errors and incomplete seed sets visible. Do not average only the episodes that happened to finish. Record Minimum information Environment Exact environment ID, repository commit and local changes, robot/controller binding, task fingerprint and registered horizon. Policy Checkpoint path and SHA-256, model/adapter runtime, training-data scope and package/Base identity where applicable. Episodes Planned episode count, full seed list, success predicate output, length, errors and any retries. Observations and execution Camera preset, image dimensions/order, history offsets, normalization, state layout, control rate and chunk execution rule. Include DP’s executed chunk size. Language and scenes GR00T instruction sampling rule and per-episode instruction; background ID and manifest; complete-task stage-switching trace. Evidence Original per-episode records, summary, relevant rollout videos, aggregation code and a declaration of any recipe-to-protocol changes. Keep checkpoint-selection scores, small functional checks and canonical benchmark results in separate records. The Leaderboard continues to display the fixed manuscript snapshot; these documentation recipes do not modify its numerical results. Continue with the end-to-end tutorial , release resources , or the score protocol . ← Previous Training Next → Cross-scene evaluation

title: Configurations — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Configurations Configurations Keep environment identity, control, camera inputs and recorded data compatible across the complete workflow. Four contracts to keep together Contract Source of truth What to preserve Task identity tasks/config/collection_targets.py ↗ The 10 complete tasks, 30 stage tasks and chosen end effector. Embodiment tasks/config/hands.py ↗ Robot UID, controller, ordered joints and action width. Simulation tasks/config/sim_profiles.py ↗ Control frequency, physics backend and task-specific episode horizon. Policy input utils/pixel_cameras.py ↗ Camera preset, resolution, preprocessing and state channel order. Run examples from the public repository root after installation . A configuration copied from another task can silently change the experiment even when the policy still produces an action of the right shape. Resolve the selected stage from utils.dex_scene_eval import registered_task_settings from utils.dex_tasks import resolve_dex_task env_id = "CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1" settings = registered_task_settings(env_id) task = resolve_dex_task(env_id) print(settings) print(task.robot_uids, task.max_episode_steps, task.action_dim) registered_task_settings resolves a canonical stage's robot, pd_joint_pos controller and registered time limit without constructing a simulator. The Sharpa VLA registry in utils/dex_tasks.py ↗ also carries joint layouts and instructions. For complete tasks and non-Sharpa hands, check the task registration and tasks/config/hands.py ↗ instead of assuming a Sharpa-only adapter supports them. Match the method, not the default viewport The released image-policy paths use a fixed family scene view and the relevant wrist view. PPO and RLPD use 128 × 128 images; ACT, Diffusion Policy, GR00T and π0.5 use 256 × 256 . The ordinary task camera can be a different view. Use the method's documented preset and renderer, not a diagnostic screenshot. ACT and Diffusion Policy additionally need the checkpoint's camera-history offsets, image normalization and state layout. The pixel RL loaders hash the camera configuration and reject an incompatible dataset or checkpoint. See utils/camera_configs.py ↗ , utils/pixel_cameras.py ↗ and the training recipes . Record the resolved experiment Save the source commit and local changes, current environment ID, robot UID, controller, backend, horizon, seed list, observation schema and camera configuration. Add the checkpoint hash, instruction-sampling rule and action normalization. Preserve the dataset integrity certificate rather than editing it to fit a changed environment. For native-scene runs, save env.unwrapped.eval_background_manifest . Fingerprint compatibility includes explicitly measured, record-neutral transitions in tasks/config/fingerprint_lineage.py ↗ ; a task change that alters recorded behavior is not made compatible by renaming its fingerprint. Continue with Evaluation and the reproduction record . ← Previous Resources & release status Next → End effectors

title: Policy integration — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Policy integration Policy integration Connect a policy to the released environment without changing its input, action or success contract. Start from an existing evaluator The six scored methods already have evaluation entry points. Prefer those paths when reproducing a released checkpoint: they restore model-specific image processing, temporal history, action execution and result recording. Evaluation provides the commands; train/TRAIN_EVAL.md ↗ describes ACT, Diffusion Policy, PPO and RLPD. A new policy needs an explicit adapter. Define which observations it consumes, how its outputs become controller targets, when a chunk is refreshed, and which reset event clears its state. Merely matching the tensor width does not establish a compatible policy. Discover the native interface import gymnasium as gym import tasks from utils.dex_scene_eval import registered_task_settings env_id = "OfficeDeskClickMouse-Sharpa-v1" env = gym.make(env_id, **registered_task_settings(env_id), obs_mode="state", num_envs=1, sim_backend="physx_cpu") try: observation, info = env.reset(seed=10001) print(env.observation_space) print(env.action_space) finally: env.close() This is an environment-interface check, not a learned-policy score. Image agents must construct their method's fixed camera rig before creating the environment. Read task state and channel names from the selected environment and dataset metadata; object-state fields must not leak into an image policy that was trained without them. Keep model coordinates separate from joint targets The released Sharpa demonstrations store absolute pd_joint_pos targets in radians: 29 values for one arm and hand, 58 for both. For the dual robot the controller order is left arm, right arm, left hand, right hand. Use utils/dex_tasks.py ↗ and the live controller binding to obtain the actual named layout. RLPD's residual actions, GR00T's modality transforms and π0.5's asynchronous queue are model interfaces, not changes to the task's native controller. Preserve their conversions rather than sending normalized or relative outputs straight to env.step . π0.5 checks named joints, cameras and the controller through utils/pi05_utils/binding.py ↗ . Reset model state and retain every outcome Clear action queues, recurrent state, temporal ensembles and instruction caches on every environment reset. Handle termination and time limits separately. Accumulate whether the task's info["success"] became true during the episode; also retain final-step success when diagnosing replay, since the two can differ. Use the registered horizon for a full benchmark run and save one record per requested seed. A short wiring run, a random action sample or an infrastructure error is not a policy score. Review the protocol and checkpoint limitations before comparing your result with the leaderboard . ← Previous End effectors Next → Data & replay

title: Cross-scene evaluation — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Cross-scene evaluation Cross-scene evaluation Evaluate a frozen policy across the three named native kitchen scenes while preserving the task definition. Three scenes, one frozen checkpoint Scene ID Native surface robocasa_l3_s1 Light wood kitchen island robocasa_l3_s2 Blue kitchen stone island robocasa_l3_s6 Warm wood kitchen stone island The published scene track crosses 30 stages with these three backgrounds. Keep the checkpoint frozen, use the same explicit episode seeds, average within each scene, then report the mean and standard deviation across the three scene averages. These are named native scenes, not arbitrary color filters or newly sampled procedural rooms. The implementation and asset requirements are in docs/howto_cross_scene_eval.md ↗ . Install the project meshes and the required ManiSkill scene assets before rendering. Use the shared native-scene factory from utils.dex_scene_eval import BACKGROUND_IDS, make_scene_eval_env env = make_scene_eval_env( "OfficeDeskClickMouse-Sharpa-v1", scene_background=BACKGROUND_IDS[0], obs_mode="rgb", ) try: obs, info = env.reset(seed=10001) print(env.unwrapped.eval_background_manifest) finally: env.close() The shared factory enforces one CPU-physics environment, the registered robot and horizon, pd_joint_pos , reset-time reconfiguration and a fixed 256 × 256 base/wrist rig. Incompatible overrides fail explicitly. PPO and RLPD have method-specific 128 × 128 image wrappers; use their documented evaluator rather than overriding this factory's camera contract. Check placement before loading a model python utils/scene_matrix.py plan --out output/scene90 python utils/scene_matrix.py preview --index 2 --out output/scene90/preview python -m pytest -q tests/test_scene_backgrounds.py tests/test_robodex_camera_configs.py plan enumerates the 90 combinations without simulation. preview requires the rendering runtime and saves policy-camera frames, placement checks and logs without loading policy weights. Diagnostic overview cameras do not enter the policy observation. Passing a placement check neither measures policy success nor proves every future policy trajectory is collision-free. Preserve scene evidence and aggregation Save the native-scene manifest, source commit, checkpoint hash, seed list and per-episode results for every task/scene pair. Native table collision geometry differs between scenes even when the working edge and tabletop height are aligned; do not describe the operation as a purely cosmetic background replacement. The optional laboratory scene in AVAILABLE_BACKGROUND_IDS is not a fourth scene in the published three-kitchen matrix. Keep new scene experiments separately labeled. Continue with method-specific evaluation and the score definitions . ← Previous Evaluation Next → Domain randomization

title: Domain randomization — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Domain randomization Domain randomization Explore appearance and workspace variation without confusing a modified training environment with the fixed evaluation scenes. Opt in to each variation RandomizedTableSceneBuilder ↗ supports table appearance, background and lighting variation, with optional table-height changes. Defaults are inert. This procedural builder is distinct from the fixed native-kitchen scene track and does not automatically produce an official benchmark result. Follow docs/howto_randomize_scene.md ↗ for integration and docs/howto_scene_library.md ↗ for authored interiors. Record which axes are enabled, their ranges, asset sources and seeds. Make one change at a time before combining variations. Integrate the builder in a task from tasks.scene_builders import RandomizedTableSceneBuilder # Inside a task's _load_scene(self, options): self.table_scene = RandomizedTableSceneBuilder( env=self, random_table_texture=True, random_background=True, random_lighting=True, ) self.table_scene.build() This fragment belongs in a task implementation; it is not a top-level executable script. Preserve the task's existing initialization and actor placement. If you enable table-height jitter, apply the builder's per-environment table_top_offsets to every table-supported actor; the builder does not move task-added objects for you. Preserve camera and collision semantics Randomized appearances matter only when the policy receives images. Keep resolution, intrinsics, sensor order and preprocessing consistent with training. Camera pose randomization is a separate opt-in operation described by the guide; do not shift cameras accidentally while changing a background texture. The procedural background enclosure is visual and has no collision shapes. It must not be advertised as a physical obstacle. Conversely, native scene surfaces have their own geometry and collision semantics. See Cross-scene evaluation for that separate contract. Revalidate changed task builds After editing a task, rerun the functional tests and inspect representative resets and policy-camera frames. Changes to physical parameters, object placement or success predicates can invalidate existing demonstration compatibility. Use the restoration, replay and label-parity checks before reusing data. Do not alter integrity certificates to silence drift. A record-neutral fingerprint lineage must be supported by evidence, not declared merely because the task still looks similar. Keep randomized-training ablations separate from the published fixed protocol and document them with the reproduction record . ← Previous Cross-scene evaluation Next → Parallel environments

title: Parallel environments — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Parallel environments Parallel environments Scale a supported evaluator while preserving seeds, complete episode accounting and native-scene constraints. Parallelism is method-specific The public PPO pixel trainer supports batched GPU physics for rollout collection. RLPD's documented pixel setting uses a single environment. Native-scene evaluation requires one CPU-physics environment per task/background pair. There is no universal environment count that every task, renderer or policy supports. Read train/TRAIN_EVAL.md ↗ and your trainer's --help before increasing concurrency. More environments increase image buffers, renderer memory and bookkeeping requirements; a smaller successful smoke test is preferable to treating capacity as guaranteed. Split independent scene combinations python utils/scene_matrix.py plan --out output/scene90 python utils/scene_matrix.py preview --out output/scene90/preview --shard 0 --shards 3 python utils/scene_matrix.py preview --out output/scene90/preview --shard 1 --shards 3 python utils/scene_matrix.py preview --out output/scene90/preview --shard 2 --shards 3 These commands partition the placement-preview matrix; they do not evaluate a policy. Launch shards independently on allocated resources. utils/scene_matrix.py ↗ uses isolated child processes, preserves failure logs, and supports --resume for matching scene source hashes and seeds. Never score only the surviving workers The replay validator can distribute episodes with --jobs . A missing worker is not a failed policy episode and is not permission to report a rate over the survivors. An !! INCOMPLETE result withholds a valid release rate until the requested episodes are accounted for. See data_gen/replay/README.md ↗ and Data & replay . For learned-policy evaluation, retain the requested seed list, completed attempts and infrastructure failures so a resumed job cannot silently change the denominator. Keep the experimental unit unchanged Do not reset an unfinished episode just because a neighboring vector environment completed. Preserve each task's horizon, model state, action queue and seed. Image-policy observations must retain the checkpoint's fixed camera configuration when batching. Keep one result directory per method, checkpoint, task and scene identity. Aggregate after all expected records exist, not by averaging worker percentages with different sample counts. The evaluation guide and reproduction checklist describe the records to save. ← Previous Domain randomization Next → Reproduction record

title: Collection background — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Collection background Collection background Understand how the released demonstrations were collected and where the public data pipeline begins. A historical collection stage, not a released interface The teleoperation stack is not released The device-specific teleoperation stack used to collect the demonstrations is not part of the public repository. This page describes collection provenance only. There are no public headset, glove, hardware-port or operator-launch commands to install from this documentation. Demonstrations were teleoperated in simulation using a Franka arm with the Sharpa dexterous hand, with absolute joint-position targets at 20 Hz. The benchmark release starts from reviewed recordings rather than exposing the collection devices as a required runtime dependency. The public pipeline starts at review and export The released tools in data_gen/recordings/README.md ↗ implement recording storage, review, certified export and replay primitives. Their outputs are LeRobot v3.0 datasets, integrity certificates and raw-recording sidecars. These components are usable independently of the unreleased device integration. data_gen/recordings/review_demos.py ↗ is the review/export entry point. Validation and release-subset selection live under data_gen/replay/README.md ↗ ; offline multi-view rendering lives under data_gen/render/README.md ↗ . Use the released demonstrations directly The gated SIPAIR/DexArena dataset repository ↗ contains 100 replay-successful episodes per stage task under data/sharpa/<env id>/ , plus remaining reviewed recordings under data_append/ . Request access and authenticate as described in Installation . You do not need the original collection devices to inspect, restore, render or train on these recordings. The end-to-end tutorial begins with downloading an existing dataset; Data & replay explains its schema and the checks every release episode passed. Collecting new data changes the provenance If you build your own collection interface, preserve the live robot's joint names, controller order, simulator state and episode identity. New recordings need their own review, restoration, action-replay and label-parity checks. A visually plausible playback is not an integrity certificate or a replay-success result. Record the collection code revision and changed task definitions. Do not label a new dataset as the official release or overwrite an existing certificate. Consult the configuration contract and reproduction record . ← Previous Data & replay Next → Training

title: End effectors — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / End effectors End effectors Choose among the four registered end effectors while keeping released-data coverage and joint layouts explicit. Four variants of each task Every task registers one environment ID for each of Sharpa, Wuji, XHand and Gripper : <Task>-<Hand>-v1 . The 40 task definitions therefore register 160 environment IDs. The end-effector and robot-UID rules live in tasks/config/hands.py ↗ ; the task list lives in tasks/config/collection_targets.py ↗ . The 40 definitions are 10 complete tasks and their 30 stages, not 160 distinct task objectives. See task table ↗ for each task's arm side and registered horizon. Resolve the robot for a chosen hand from tasks.config.hands import HANDS, env_id, robot_uid for hand in HANDS: print(env_id("DrawerPlugOpenDrawer", hand), robot_uid(hand, "left")) Use left , right or both according to the task registration. Do not attach a robot from a different stage merely because the objects belong to the same family. The robot agents and controller implementations are under tasks/robots/__init__.py ↗ . Published data and baselines use Sharpa The released demonstration sets and reported baseline scores use the Sharpa hand. The current dataset and checkpoint release ↗ must not be presented as a matched demonstration set for all four end effectors. Training a different hand requires compatible data, controller binding and a clearly labeled evaluation. Sharpa has 29 absolute joint targets for one arm/hand and 58 for the bimanual robot. These dimensions are not universal across hands. Read the live action space and ordered joint names for your robot; never pad, truncate or reuse a Sharpa checkpoint without an explicit embodiment adapter. Changing a hand is a separate experiment Robot geometry, contact behavior, controller gains and state/action normalization can all change with the end effector. Revalidate the environment reset, mesh loading and success predicates, then record the source revision and hand variant with every result. Use Policy integration for adapter requirements, Configurations for camera and control contracts, and Data & replay before claiming a demonstration is compatible with the modified robot. ← Previous Configurations Next → Policy integration

title: Troubleshooting — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Troubleshooting Troubleshooting Diagnose installation, artifact access, rendering and protocol mismatches before spending time on a training run. Check the checkout and dependencies first Run commands from the public repository root in the intended Python environment. Import tasks before creating a Gym environment and use the current <Task>-<Hand>-v1 ID. The installation guide pins Gymnasium 0.29.1 and LeRobot 0.4.0; newer dependency resolution is not automatically equivalent. The functional tests need no downloaded demonstrations or checkpoints. They check task tables, contracts and baseline interfaces, not policy success. Keep their output and source revision when reporting a regression. python -m pip show torch mani_skill gymnasium lerobot python -m pytest tests -q Dataset access or missing meshes Symptom What to check Hub download returns 401/403 Request access to the gated dataset repository ↗ and run hf auth login in the environment performing the download. Never paste your token into a bug report. Missing task-object mesh Download assets/** with --local-dir tasks ; files should be under tasks/assets/task_object_meshes/ , not an extra nested assets directory. Checkpoint not found Use the exact published method directory. ACT/DP use current task IDs; π0.5 packages may keep their trained legacy directory names while evaluation takes the current ID. GR00T backbone access fails Accept the gated backbone terms or use the documented local backbone path. GR00T has its own runtime and model-access requirements. GPU, Vulkan and camera failures CPU physics does not eliminate the GPU/Vulkan requirement for rendering. Confirm the NVIDIA driver and a PyTorch wheel supporting your GPU. RTX 50-series hardware needs the compatible CUDA build described in Installation. A blank viewport should be fixed before interpreting any policy score. Tasks whose recordings change render-body visibility need the CPU path for pixel-demo rendering; the training guide names the known example. Reduce render batch size or continue with the renderer's supported chunking options rather than changing the camera preset to make a failing run fit. pixel-rendering guide ↗ documents these restrictions. Fingerprint drift and weak checkpoint results fingerprint DRIFT means the recording and task build are not admitted as compatible. The validators resolve the measured record-neutral lineages in tasks/config/fingerprint_lineage.py ↗ ; other changed task behavior remains incompatible. An !! INCOMPLETE worker result is not a release-success rate. If a checkpoint loads but performs poorly, verify the camera preset, image size, ordered state channels, horizon, seed list and action processing before changing the policy. DP execution chunk size and GR00T instruction sampling materially affect the protocol. See Evaluation for method-specific settings and distinctions between paper and released checkpoints. Prepare a minimal, public-safe report Include the exact command with secrets removed, source commit, current environment ID, dependency versions, relevant traceback and the smallest reproducible case. Do not upload access tokens, private filesystem paths or complete gated artifacts. Open an issue in the official code repository ↗ . For result reproducibility, include the experiment record and distinguish a functional smoke test from a full evaluation. ← Previous Reproduction record Next → Citation

title: Reproduction record — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Reproduction record Reproduction record Save enough evidence for another researcher to identify the task, checkpoint, data and protocol behind a result. A checklist, not a submission portal Community submission intake is not open The current leaderboard presents the supplied manuscript baselines. This page describes reproducibility records; it does not provide an upload endpoint, announce an open competition or promise inclusion in a public ranking. Keep experiments from different task revisions, checkpoints, instruction protocols or data subsets separately labeled. The leaderboard protocol defines how the three reported tracks are aggregated. Record identity before running Record Include Source and task Repository commit and local changes; current environment ID and hand; task fingerprint and any resolved lineage. Model Method, checkpoint path and hash, training data subset, model/runtime versions and any pretrained Base dependency. Environment Robot UID, controller, physics backend, registered horizon, reset policy and native-scene manifest when relevant. Policy inputs and actions Camera preset and resolution, preprocessing, temporal offsets, state channel names, normalization and action execution rule. Evaluation Requested seed list, number of complete episodes, instruction sampling, scene IDs and result-directory identity. Do not replace a changed task fingerprint with the release fingerprint. Record-neutral compatibility is handled by tasks/config/fingerprint_lineage.py ↗ and must have evidence behind it. Retain per-episode evidence Save every requested episode's seed, success-at-any-step result, length and failure or infrastructure-error status. Preserve the evaluator CSV or episodes.jsonl , its summary, run command and diagnostic videos where available. A completed denominator matters more than an attractive aggregate percentage. Identify ACT/DP execution settings, PPO/RLPD rendered demonstration dependencies, GR00T canonical versus registered instruction sampling and π0.5 Base/package hashes. The released GR00T multi-instruction checkpoints are not the paper's single-instruction checkpoints; do not label one as a reproduction of the other. Aggregate only comparable runs Average the stage-level success rates over the 30 canonical stages. For cross-scene results, calculate each scene's average first and then the mean and standard deviation across the three named scenes. Long-horizon results concern the 10 complete sequences from one reset, not the mean or product of standalone stage scores. Keep partial diagnostic runs and workstation measurements out of these headline aggregates. Report all deviations from the fixed task, camera, horizon and seed protocol. Read Evaluation for released-package limitations and Citation for the canonical paper reference. ← Previous Parallel environments Next → Troubleshooting

title: Leaderboard protocol — DexArena
text: Leaderboard Score protocol Three evaluation tracks, explicit aggregation and a reproducible evidence trail. Manuscript baselines, not a verified community leaderboard The current scores are the six paper baselines. Public submission intake, remote execution and independent verification are not yet available. Evaluation units 01 Stage execution 30 stages × 50 episodes in the training scene. Each stage starts from its own valid reset distribution. 02 Cross-scene 30 stages × 3 native scenes × 50 episodes. Freeze the policy; retain the background manifest for every run. 03 Long-horizon 10 sequences × 50 episodes. Reset once per episode, never between stages; measure final sequence completion. How scores are aggregated Stage and long-horizon averages weight tasks equally. For cross-scene results, average stage success within each scene first, then report the mean and standard deviation across the three scene averages. The ± value is scene variation, not a training-seed confidence interval. The original manuscript records ACT/DP stage seeds 50000–50049 and GR00T seeds 10001–10050. New comparison sweeps should use matched episode seeds across methods and record the manifest; do not imply the paper used identical seed ranges for every method. Keep task horizons and physical success predicates fixed. Persistent hold counters or latches are part of the task definition. π0.5 switches stage models for composition; GR00T uses a pooled task model with stage instructions. Reproduction package Identity Environment/task revision, robot UID, controller, horizon and seeds. Policy Checkpoint hash, adapter revision, training-data scope and observation preprocessing. Scenes Background IDs, camera profile and source/geometry manifests. Outcomes Per-episode success, steps, stage trace, logs, videos and aggregation script. Explore results ↗ Rollouts & evidence ↗ Preparation checklist ↗
